questions.q: According to the lesson, how should you treat the first answer an assistant gives you?
options: As the finished product, ready to use as is
As proof your prompt failed if it isn't perfect
As a draft you can steer with follow-ups
As a guess you should always throw away
questions.explain: The first answer is a draft. The real value comes from specific follow-ups that build on the conversation instead of starting over.

questions.q: An answer is close, but the ending sounds too salesy. What's the best next step?
options: Reply "that's not right" and ask it to try again
Delete the chat and retype your original prompt
Open a new chat and ask the same question there
Say what to keep and that the ending sounds salesy
questions.explain: Specific feedback about what to keep and what's wrong beats vague feedback, and following up keeps the context you've already built.

questions.q: Your chat has become long and muddled, but you want to keep working on the same project. What should you do?
options: Ask it to summarize the conversation, then paste that into a new chat
Keep adding corrections in the same chat until it gets back on track
Start a new chat with no background and re-explain everything from memory
Tell the assistant to forget everything and carry on in the same chat
questions.explain: A long, muddled conversation is a sign to start a new chat. Asking the old chat to summarize your preferences and decisions first lets you carry the context over.
